job.style: a short story with Indian characters in everyday life

passage: Rohan and his grandfather sat under a banyan tree near the ruins of Pataliputra, the ancient capital of the Mauryan Empire. Grandfather pointed to a massive stone pillar nearby. 'Look at these carvings, Rohan,' he said. 'These are inscriptions, engraved on stone so they would last for centuries, unlike paper which decays quickly.' Rohan touched the rough surface. 'Did Chanakya write these?' he asked. Grandfather smiled, 'No, Chanakya was the wise advisor who helped Chandragupta Maurya build the empire, but Ashoka ordered these inscriptions.' Rohan asked about the Kalinga war. 'Was it a small fight?' Grandfather shook his head, 'Kalinga was a powerful kingdom. The war was so brutal that it changed Ashoka forever, leading him to abandon violence.' Rohan wondered if Ashoka forced people to become Buddhists. 'Not exactly,' Grandfather explained. 'Ashoka promoted Dhamma, a set of moral principles for living in harmony. He encouraged people to follow these values, but he did not force anyone to adopt a specific religion or make Buddhism the state religion.' Rohan looked at the pillar with new respect, understanding that the empire was built on strategy, reflection, and a desire for peace rather than just conquest.

items.evidence: 'These are inscriptions, engraved on stone so they would last for centuries, unlike paper which decays quickly.'
items.q: Why were Mauryan inscriptions carved on stone pillars?
options: Stone lasts much longer than paper
Paper was not known in ancient India
Stone was easier to carve than paper
Kings wanted to write in Sanskrit only
items.explain: Stone lasts for centuries, while paper decays quickly, so the messages would survive.

wrong.why: thinks inscriptions were written on paper, so paper must not exist
picks a plausible but unsupported reason about ease
thinks all inscriptions were in Sanskrit

items.evidence: Grandfather smiled, 'No, Chanakya was the wise advisor who helped Chandragupta Maurya build the empire, but Ashoka ordered these inscriptions.'
items.q: What was Chanakya's role compared with Ashoka's role in the Mauryan Empire?
options: Chanakya advised a king; Ashoka ordered the pillars
Chanakya ruled as king; Ashoka advised him
Chanakya ordered the pillars; Ashoka advised a king
Chanakya was Ashoka's father; Ashoka was his heir
items.explain: Chanakya was an advisor who helped Chandragupta; Ashoka was the king who ordered the inscriptions.

wrong.why: mixes up who ordered the inscriptions
thinks Chandragupta was Ashoka's son and heir, mixing up family ties

items.evidence: Grandfather shook his head, 'Kalinga was a powerful kingdom. The war was so brutal that it changed Ashoka forever, leading him to abandon violence.'
items.q: Why did the Kalinga war change Ashoka so deeply?
options: Its brutal fighting made him give up violence
It was an easy win that made him proud
It was a small fight he soon forgot
It made him send soldiers to punish rebels
items.explain: The war was so brutal that Ashoka turned away from violence, so it changed him.

wrong.why: thinks Kalinga was a small, unimportant fight
thinks Ashoka's officers were soldiers punishing rebels

items.evidence: He encouraged people to follow these values, but he did not force anyone to adopt a specific religion or make Buddhism the state religion.
items.q: A farmer in Ashoka's empire follows another faith. What would Dhamma ask of him?
options: To live by moral values in harmony
To give up his faith and become Buddhist
To join the army and fight in wars
To pay a tax for keeping his faith
items.explain: Dhamma was a set of moral values for harmony; Ashoka forced no one to change religion.
